explanations.statement: BYD's within-segment mix in battery electric fell from 100.00% (P4) to 62.63% (L4), a drop of 37.37 percentage points, indicating BYD's BEV registrations are no longer its sole volume source as the brand's share of its own segment changed.
Ford's battery electric mix rose from 3.05% (P4) to 15.28% (L4), a gain of 12.23 percentage points, the largest upward mix shift among the anomalies.
Volkswagen's battery electric mix increased from 10.69% (P4) to 18.65% (L4), a gain of 7.96 percentage points, while its within-segment share also rose from 5.63% to 7.81%.
MG's battery electric mix fell from 30.05% (P4) to 22.85% (L4), a decline of 7.20 percentage points, and its within-segment share fell from 7.81% to 4.14%, a decline of 3.67 percentage points.

Tesla's total share edged up while its battery electric segment share fell, with a total-share change of 0.15 percentage points against a segment-share change of -2.76 percentage points, a divergence between total and within-segment performance.

alternative_explanations.statement: BYD's BEV volume actually declined, reducing its segment share, independent of non-BEV growth

explanations.statement: BYD's battery-electric share of its own registrations fell sharply from 91.46% in the prior four quarters to 58.35% in the last four quarters, indicating a large shift toward non-BEV fuel types within BYD's mix.

BYD's BEV segment share rose from 2.11% to 6.30% while its total share fell from 0.44% to 2.47%, so its total share gain reflects BEV segment growth as a share of the BEV market rather than overall brand growth.
Ford's battery-electric mix rose from 8.45% to 24.33%, a 15.88 percentage point increase, even though Ford's total share was roughly flat (5.56% to 5.79%).
Kia's total share fell slightly while its BEV segment share rose, a divergence between total and within-segment performance.
MG's total share was essentially flat while its BEV segment share fell by 2.04 percentage points, a divergence between total and within-segment performance.

alternative_explanations.statement: BYD's BEV registrations fell in absolute terms while non-BEV held steady, giving the same mix change
A single large fleet or rental order shifted the mix temporarily

assumptions.statement: BYD's non-BEV registrations grew in the L4 window relative to P4
Channel mix did not shift dramatically between fuel types

conditions: BYD continues to register both BEV and non-BEV vehicles in GB
No change in BYD's BEV model availability

mechanism.cause: Expansion of non-BEV powertrain offerings by BYD in GB
mechanism.pathway: Non-BEV registrations grow faster than BEV registrations within BYD's mix

model_request.rationale: Level baseline for BYD mix over the test window with no structural assumptions.

hypotheses.novelty_claim: Attributes the BEV mix decline specifically to BYD's non-BEV range expansion rather than to overall demand weakness.

observable_implications.description: BYD's BEV mix in the next two quarters stays below its L4 value of 58.35%
observable_implications.would_refute_if: BYD's BEV mix rises back above 58.35% in both test quarters

observable_implications.description: BYD's BEV segment share in the next two quarters exceeds its L4 value of 6.30%
observable_implications.would_refute_if: BYD's BEV segment share falls below 6.30% in the test window

hypotheses.refutation_criteria: BYD's BEV mix recovers toward 91.46% in the test window, or BYD's BEV segment share falls back toward its P4 level of 2.11%.
hypotheses.statement: BYD's falling BEV mix reflects a deliberate expansion of its hybrid and petrol range into the UK fleet and retail channels, which dilutes BEV share without reducing its BEV registrations as a share of the BEV market.
